statement: A practitioner's published protocol (Blueprint, Medicine 3.0, a supplement stack) is a recipe, not evidence of efficacy. The protocol's existence/popularity carries zero evidentiary weight; each component must be graded against its own primary source.
effect_size: N/A (methodological rule)

provenance.primary: 06-evidence/SCHEMA.md hard rules

confidence_notes: Operationalizes the SCHEMA rule: 'a practitioner's name attached to a claim is provenance, not evidence.' Every claim below honors this separation.

statement: Bryan Johnson's Blueprint protocol slows his measured 'pace of aging' (DunedinPACE-style) to below 1.0 and improves numerous personal biomarkers.
effect_size: Self-reported pace-of-aging <1.0; various biomarker improvements (single subject)

provenance.primary: blueprint.bryanjohnson.com self-published data; Rejuvenation Olympics leaderboard

confidence_notes: N=1, no control, no randomization, dozens of simultaneous interventions → no component-level causal inference. Commercial COI (sells the stack). The dataset's value is transparency, not proof.

statement: Bryan Johnson discontinued weekly rapamycin (~2024) after reporting no net benefit and side effects, despite rapamycin's strong mouse-lifespan data.
effect_size: Self-reported: discontinued; no perceived benefit, adverse effects (e.g. lipid/glucose/soft-tissue issues)

provenance.primary: Bryan Johnson public statements / Blueprint updates 2024

confidence_notes: A self-reported NEGATIVE — more informative than the marketing positives. Consistent with PEARL (NCT04488601) showing only modest surrogate signal. Animal lifespan benefit has NOT translated to a clear personal human benefit here.

statement: Higher cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2max) is associated with substantially lower all-cause mortality, with no observed upper limit of benefit; the elite-vs-low difference rivals or exceeds that of major clinical risk factors.
effect_size: Elite vs low fitness: HR ~0.20 for all-cause mortality (~5x risk gradient); low fitness adjusted HR ~5 vs elite

provenance.primary: Mandsager et al., JAMA Network Open 2018

confidence_notes: Observational — strong, consistent gradient but residual confounding (reverse causation: sick people exercise less) not fully excluded. This is the single strongest-evidence pillar of the Attia framework. Domain E.

statement: Higher muscle strength (e.g. grip strength) and muscle mass are associated with lower all-cause mortality in older adults.
effect_size: Grip strength inversely associated with mortality (per-5kg-decrease HR ~1.16 all-cause, PURE study)

provenance.primary: Leong et al., Lancet 2015 (grip strength & mortality)

confidence_notes: Grip strength is a biomarker/proxy of total strength and frailty, associated not proven-causal. Supports training-for-reserve heuristic. Domain E.

statement: Higher protein intake (~1.6-2.2 g/kg/day) maximizes muscle protein synthesis and helps preserve lean mass with age, supporting lower frailty/mortality risk in older adults.
effect_size: MPS plateaus ~1.6 g/kg/day (Morton meta); muscle preservation benefit in elderly
population: Resistance-training adults (Morton 2018 meta of RCTs); elderly cohorts

provenance.primary: Morton et al., Br J Sports Med 2018 (protein RCT meta); Stuart Phillips body of work

confidence_notes: DIRECTLY CONFLICTS with the Longo/IGF-1/mTOR protein-restriction-for-longevity position (animal+epi tier). Likely age- and context-dependent (Attia/Phillips champion elderly muscle; Longo champions mid-life mTOR restraint). See 06-evidence/CONFLICTS.md conflict-protein-mtor-longevity — status OPEN.

statement: High-dose omega-3 (EPA/DHA) supplementation improves the omega-3 index and lowers triglycerides/inflammation, but evidence for hard cardiovascular/mortality outcomes is mixed.
effect_size: Modest CV event reduction in some meta-analyses (esp. high-dose EPA, REDUCE-IT); null in others (VITAL, STRENGTH primary)
population: Multiple large RCTs / meta-analyses (VITAL n=25,871; REDUCE-IT n=8,179; STRENGTH)

provenance.primary: Manson et al. NEJM 2019 (VITAL, null); Bhatt et al. NEJM 2019 (REDUCE-IT, positive icosapent ethyl)

confidence_notes: A clean MIXED case: surrogate/biomarker benefits real; hard-outcome benefit depends on dose, formulation (EPA vs EPA+DHA), and baseline risk. Do not present as settled. Domain D/L.

statement: Vitamin D3 supplementation corrects deficiency, but large RCTs show no reduction in all-cause mortality, cancer, or CVD in already-replete general populations.
effect_size: VITAL: no significant reduction in invasive cancer or major CV events; some signal for cancer mortality on follow-up

provenance.primary: Manson et al., NEJM 2019 (VITAL)

confidence_notes: Benefit concentrated in deficient/low-baseline individuals; supplementing the already-replete shows little hard-outcome effect. Surrogate (serum 25-OH-D) easily raised; outcome benefit limited. Domain D/L.

statement: Sulforaphane (from broccoli sprouts) activates the Nrf2 pathway, inducing phase-II antioxidant/detoxification enzymes.
effect_size: Robust Nrf2/ARE induction; downstream human clinical-outcome benefit largely unproven
population: Human/animal mechanistic + small clinical studies (e.g. airway/autism/detox pilots)

provenance.primary: Fahey/Talalay sulforaphane Nrf2 body of work

confidence_notes: MECHANISM, not outcome — flagged explicitly per SCHEMA (a mechanism claim may never be presented as an outcome). Strong biology, thin hard-endpoint human data. Domain D.

statement: Frequent sauna use (4-7x/week) is associated with lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.
effect_size: HR ~0.60 all-cause mortality (4-7x/week vs 1x/week)

provenance.primary: Laukkanen et al., JAMA Intern Med 2015

confidence_notes: Observational; healthy-user and reverse-causation not fully excluded (sicker people sauna less). Same study cited as the H-thermal SCHEMA example. Domain H.

statement: Viewing outdoor light early in the day (~10-30 min within ~1h of waking) advances/sets the circadian clock and supports the morning cortisol pulse via melanopsin ipRGC -> SCN signaling.
effect_size: Robust circadian phase-setting via short-wavelength-sensitive ipRGCs; outdoor lux (1k-100k) >> indoor

provenance.primary: Brainard 2001 / Berson 2002 ipRGC + melanopsin action spectrum; popularized by Huberman Lab

confidence_notes: MECHANISM (circadian entrainment), well established; the specific 'morning sunlight cures X' OUTCOME framing is heuristic. Cross-ref I-claims light-melatonin-action-spectrum, room-light-melatonin-suppression. Domain I.

statement: Delaying caffeine ~90-120 min after waking (to let residual adenosine clear) reduces the afternoon energy crash.
effect_size: No controlled trial of the 'delay' benefit; adenosine-antagonism mechanism of caffeine is established

provenance.primary: Huberman Lab podcast (mechanistic argument); caffeine-adenosine pharmacology

confidence_notes: Mechanism real (caffeine blocks adenosine receptors), but the specific timing benefit is a low-risk heuristic with essentially no RCT. One of the items most uniquely 'his' and among the thinnest-evidence.

statement: Non-Sleep Deep Rest (NSDR) / yoga nidra (10-20 min guided body-scan relaxation) restores alertness/dopamine and can offset poor sleep.
effect_size: Small early studies on yoga nidra (mood, autonomic, striatal dopamine pilot); limited rigor

provenance.primary: Kjaer 2002 (yoga nidra striatal dopamine PET, n small); Huberman 'NSDR' branding/aggregation

confidence_notes: NSDR is an umbrella term Huberman coined; the underlying practices have small/early evidence. Low-risk; not an established clinical intervention. Overlaps G-domain slow-breathing/relaxation mechanisms.

statement: Daily hydration ~0.5 oz fluid/lb body weight, and during hard exercise ~bodyweight(lb)/30 oz every 15 min ('the Galpin Equation'), optimizes performance hydration.
effect_size: Practical heuristic; broadly consistent with sweat-rate-based fluid-replacement guidance (e.g. ACSM) but not a trial-derived formula

provenance.primary: Andy Galpin via Huberman Lab guest series; hydration/sweat-rate exercise-physiology literature

confidence_notes: Reasonable, mechanism-consistent heuristic for individualizing fluid intake; the specific numbers are a usable rule of thumb, NOT an outcome-validated dose. Over-drinking risk (hyponatremia) at the high end during ultra-endurance.

statement: A lower sitting-rising test (SRT) score - needing more hand/knee support to sit on and rise from the floor - is associated with substantially higher all-cause mortality in adults aged 51-80.
effect_size: Lowest SRT band (0-3) vs highest (8-10): ~5-6x higher all-cause mortality; each point ~21% lower mortality risk

provenance.primary: Brito et al., Eur J Prev Cardiol 2014

confidence_notes: Observational; SRT is a composite BIOMARKER of strength + balance + flexibility + body composition. Predictive association - NOT evidence that practicing the test changes mortality. Healthy-user/reverse-causation not excluded. Domain E/F.

statement: Greater sedentary (sitting) time is associated with higher all-cause mortality, but the association is substantially attenuated - sometimes eliminated - after adjusting for total moderate-to-vigorous physical activity.
effect_size: High sitting + low activity: elevated HR; ~60-75 min/day MVPA appears to offset the mortality association of high sitting (harmonized meta)
population: Harmonized meta-analyses (>1 million adults, Ekelund 2016/2019); Whitehall II

provenance.primary: Ekelund et al., Lancet 2016 (harmonized meta); van der Ploeg/Whitehall II

confidence_notes: MIXED: sitting is partly a proxy for low activity, not a clean independent exposure. 'Sitting is the new smoking' is overstated. Breaking up sitting + total activity is the defensible message. Domain E.

statement: McGill's 'Big 3' (modified curl-up, side bridge, bird dog) plus spine-sparing technique build core endurance/stiffness at low lumbar disc load and improve pain/function in chronic non-specific low-back pain.
effect_size: Small RCT(s): pain + functional-disability improvement comparable to (some measures favoring) conventional physiotherapy
population: Small RCTs in chronic non-specific low-back pain + McGill's spine-load/EMG biomechanics lab work

provenance.primary: McGill spine-biomechanics body of work; small McGill-stabilization RCTs (e.g. PMC5908986)

confidence_notes: Spine-sparing biomechanics (low disc load, anti-repeated-flexion) are mechanistically strong; clinical trials are small and show comparability-to-PT, not decisive superiority. Back-pain management, NOT a longevity claim. Domain F.

statement: The BOLT (Body Oxygen Level Test) breath-hold-to-first-urge measures CO2 sensitivity/breathing tolerance, and McKeown's cutoffs (<25s dysfunctional, ~40s goal) predict breathing efficiency and performance/health.
effect_size: Breath-hold time does index CO2 tolerance; the specific 25/40s cutoffs and their health/performance predictive validity are a proprietary heuristic, not independently validated

provenance.primary: Patrick McKeown, The Oxygen Advantage / oxygenadvantage.com

confidence_notes: Face-valid measure of breath-hold/CO2 tolerance; the branded cutoffs as health/performance predictors are heuristic, not RCT-validated. Treat as a program target, not a clinical threshold. Cross-ref G bohr-effect-co2-tolerance. Domain G.

statement: Habitual winter swimmers (combining regular cold-water immersion and sauna for >=2 years) show altered brown-fat thermoregulation and markedly higher cold-induced thermogenesis than controls.
effect_size: Cold-induced energy expenditure substantially elevated in winter-swimmers vs controls; altered BAT thermoregulatory pattern
population: n~8 winter-swimming men vs n~8 controls (small, cross-sectional)

provenance.primary: Soberg et al., Cell Reports Medicine 2021 (PMID 34755128)

confidence_notes: Small, CROSS-SECTIONAL, trained men, cold+heat bundled - generates the thermogenesis mechanism; does NOT prove a dose causes metabolic-health outcomes. Cross-ref H cold-activated-bat-adult-humans, shivering-vs-nonshivering-thermogenesis. Domain H.

statement: ~11 minutes/week of deliberate cold exposure split across sessions, 'ending on cold', is a sufficient minimum dose to stimulate brown-fat thermogenesis and metabolic benefit ('the Soeberg Principle').
effect_size: Practitioner-distilled minimum-threshold heuristic; not a trial-derived dose tied to a health OUTCOME

provenance.primary: Susanna Soberg, Winter Swimming / Soeberg Institute; synthesis over her + adjacent cold literature

confidence_notes: The '11 min/week + end on cold' figure is a usable heuristic, NOT an outcome-validated dose. Note: the cold-acclimation insulin-sensitivity OUTCOME (H cold-acclimation-insulin-sensitivity-t2d) came from a 6h/day x10-day protocol, not 11 min/week - keep dose<->evidence honest. Domain H.

statement: Resveratrol acts as a direct SIRT1 activator that drives anti-aging benefits.
effect_size: Pfizer/Amgen: in-vitro SIRT1 'activation' was a fluorophore-substrate assay artifact; GSK discontinued SRT501 (2010); no human anti-aging outcome
population: In-vitro biochemistry + failed clinical development (Sirtris/GSK SRT501)

provenance.primary: Pacholec et al., J Biol Chem 2010 (SRT1720/resveratrol not direct SIRT1 activators); Beher 2009; GSK Sirtris discontinuation

confidence_notes: CONTESTED. The direct-activation mechanism is disputed as an assay artifact; Sinclair contests the reading. GSK bought Sirtris ~$720M (2008), discontinued SRT501 (2010). No human longevity outcome for resveratrol. Canonical mechanism-hype example. Domain B.

statement: David Sinclair's personal longevity stack (NMN, resveratrol, metformin, TRE, plus others) slows or reverses his aging.
effect_size: N=1, no control, no published personal outcome data; many simultaneous interventions

provenance.primary: David Sinclair public statements / Lifespan podcast

confidence_notes: N=1 advocacy with DENSE financial COI (founder/equity across longevity ventures). 'NMN raises NAD+' (surrogate, B nad-precursor-nr-human-surrogate) is routinely upgraded to 'reverses aging' (outcome, unproven) - the canonical SCHEMA mechanism!=outcome violation. Indexed, not endorsed.

statement: Valter Longo's 'Longevity Diet' (pescetarian, mostly-plant, age-adjusted lower mid-life protein, ~12h eating window) plus periodic 5-day fasting-mimicking-diet cycles promotes healthy longevity.
effect_size: Composite of CR/fasting/IGF-1 + Mediterranean evidence; component RCTs are surrogate-marker (FMD risk markers), plus animal + epi; no human-longevity-endpoint trial of the whole pattern
population: Synthesis: FMD RCT (n~100), IGF-1 epi (NHANES), mouse lifespan, PREDIMED

provenance.primary: Longo, The Longevity Diet; Wei et al. Sci Transl Med 2017 (FMD RCT); Levine/Longo 2014 Cell Metab (protein-IGF1)

confidence_notes: Most trial-anchored protocol in this set, but still mostly surrogate/animal, NOT human-longevity outcome. The mid-life protein-restriction stance is the direct counterweight to Attia/Galpin/Phillips (conflict-protein-mtor-longevity, OPEN). Cross-ref D fmd-human-risk-markers, protein-igf1-age-dependent-mortality. COI: ProLon/L-Nutra. Domain D.
